item.text:
**7B.10 — Félix Tshisekedi (2024)**  
**Overall:** Mostly negative. There is some real evidence of technocratic staffing and formal oversight, but the dominant pattern is weak candor about performance, tolerance of impunity, and repeated use of coercive state power against critics and independent information.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs | Index |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| *DR Congo president appoints country’s first female prime minister* | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/ | Tshisekedi’s appointment of Judith Suminwa, a technocratic planning minister, is the clearest positive signal that he sometimes privileged competence and inclusion over pure patronage. It supports a limited trust-building reading, but only narrowly. | 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.8 | E0598 / E0521 / E0464 |
| *RDC: Minister of Finance gets a technocrat* | ACP | 2024-05-30 | https://acp.cd/economie/rdc-fwamba-likunde-un-technocrate-rompu-a-la-tete-du-ministere-des-finances-par-elysee-kakese/ | Doudou Fwamba was described as a finance technocrat with public-finance experience. This is another limited positive sign that the administration sometimes used professional staffing rather than pure loyalty politics. | 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.8 | E0600 / E0560 |
| *Le Chef de l’État a assisté à l’ouverture de la session extraordinaire du conseil supérieur de la Cour des comptes* | Présidence RDC | 2024-10-07 | https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes | The presidency said Tshisekedi backed the Court of Accounts’ control function, and the court credited him with helping revive anti-corruption oversight. This is the strongest positive evidence that he sometimes reinforced formal accountability rather than undermining it. | 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.7 | E0602 / E0572 / E0550 |
| *DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis* | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/ | Amnesty said Tshisekedi made numerous human-rights pledges but produced little to no progress, while public resources were squandered and essential services underfunded. This is strong evidence against ethical leadership that builds public trust. | 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.7, 7B.8 | E0590 / E0532 / E0434 |
| *Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts- report* | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/ | A civil-society report said CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. Even though this is not direct personal self-dealing, it is strong evidence of non-transparent resource handling around a core state process. | 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.8 | E0601 / E0594 / E0544 |
| *DRC: President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations* | Amnesty International | 2024-09-30 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/ | Amnesty says Tshisekedi’s government weaponized the judiciary, kept journalists and activists under threat, and failed to ensure a transparent investigation after Makala prison deaths and sexual violence. This is direct negative evidence for impunity and cynical abuse of state power. | 7B.10, 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.9 | E0575 / E0591 / E0577 / E0597 |
| *DR Congo: Second Term Should Focus on Rights* | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-06 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/dr-congo-second-term-should-focus-rights | HRW said Tshisekedi’s first term ended with intolerance for dissent, narrowing civic space, and little progress against corruption and impunity. This is broad negative evidence that the administration did not model ethical standards in a way that improved trust. | 7B.10, 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.9 | E0576 / E0524 / E0487 |
| *Congo President Tshisekedi draws criticism over constitutional reform plans* | Reuters | 2024-10-24 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-president-tshisekedi-draws-criticism-over-constitutional-reform-plans-2024-10-24/ | Tshisekedi launched a constitutional review process that critics said could remove term limits and open the door to a third term. That is strong evidence of opportunistic self-entrenchment and a willingness to blur or reverse formal commitments. | 7B.10, 7B.8, 4B.1 | E0603 / E0595 / E0515 |
| *Congo President Tshisekedi draws criticism over constitutional reform plans* | Reuters | 2024-10-24 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-president-tshisekedi-draws-criticism-over-constitutional-reform-plans-2024-10-24/ | The public justification was that the constitution was not aligned with current realities, but the timing and term-limit implications made the framing look disingenuous to critics. This is evidence for cynical rhetoric around political survival. | 7B.10, 7B.8 | E0603 / E0595 / E0515 |
| *Media Freedoms Should Not Be a Target in DR Congo* | Human Rights Watch | 2024-07-17 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/17/media-freedoms-should-not-be-target-dr-congo | HRW says journalists remained under pressure and media freedom was targeted. That undercuts any claim that the ruler modeled truthfulness or protected independent scrutiny. | 7B.10, 7B.7, 7B.6 | E0604 / E0537 / E0286 |
| *Media freedom under threat* | Amnesty International | 2024-05-03 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/media-freedom-under-threat/ | Amnesty reported that authorities closed down a dozen media outlets and programs and that journalist Stanis Bujakera was convicted despite weak evidence. This is direct evidence of suppressing scrutiny rather than encouraging honest public accountability. | 7B.10, 7B.7, 7B.6 | E0605 / E0577 / E0592 |

**Assessment**
- The best positive material is narrow: technocratic appointments, some fiscal-administrative professionalization, and support for the Court of Accounts.
- The stronger negative pattern is broader: disputed legitimacy, opaque procurement, media repression, judicial harassment, state-of-siege coercion, and term-limit maneuvering.
- I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of direct personal cash self-dealing by Tshisekedi or a documented first-family procurement scandal. The evidence is mostly indirect but still substantial: patronage, opacity, and self-entrenchment.
